artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and let $r\geq 1$ be an integer. A subset $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}^r$ is said to determine all directions in $\mathbb{F}^r$ if for every nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}^r$ there exist $a_1,a_2\in A$ such that $a_1-a_2$ is a (nonzero) scalar multiple of $d$; equivalently, $A$ realizes every one of the $(q^r-1)/(q-1)$ projective directions of $\mathbb{F}^r$.

A trivial counting argument shows that any such $A$ must satisfy $|A|\geq \sqrt{2}\, q^{(r-1)/2}$, and a matching upper bound $|A|\leq C\, q^{(r-1)/2}$ is achievable (for instance, by taking $A = D\times\{0,1\}$ where $D\subseteq \mathbb{F}^{r-1}$ is a difference basis of size $O(q^{(r-1)/2})$).

Determine the exact minimum value (or its precise asymptotics, including the optimal multiplicative constant) of $|A|$ over all subsets $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}^r$ that determine all directions in $\mathbb{F}^r$, as a function of $q$ and $r$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem attributed to Granville (with remarks by Konyagin). The order of magnitude $q^{(r-1)/2}$ is known (matching lower and upper bounds up to a constant), but no source found pins down the optimal constant or exact minimum size. Related literature (e.g., work on directions determined by subsets of $\mathbb{F}_q^r$) addresses qualitative results but not the precise extremal value.

status_evidence.title: On Directions Determined by Subsets of Vector Spaces over Finite Fields
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sets that determine many or all directions in F_q^r but does not give exact extremal sizes.
status_evidence.claim: Related work establishes bounds on direction-determining sets but not the optimal constant.
